newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Pipeline burst delays Indian refinery turnarounds.
newsitem.headline: Pipeline burst delays Indian refinery turnarounds.

text.p: India has delayed most of its refinery turnarounds to February-March next year due to last week's crude pipeline troubles, industry sources said on Monday.
"Once the pipeline burst, there was an immediate meeting at Oil Coordination Committee," said a source at the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.
He said most refineries will defer their maintenance shutdown to make up for a shortfall in oil products.

A fire that broke out last Thursday at a crude pipeline in Assam had resulted in the shutdown of the 2.7 million tonne a year (54,000 barrel-per-day) Bongaigaon refinery and the 3.3 million tonne (66,000-bpd) Barauni refinery.
The two refineries are due to start up on Tuesday.
A total of six Indian refineries have plans to shutdown for maintenance before March 1997 as part of this current fiscal year plans, industry sources said.

They said state-owned Indian Oil Corp Ltd (IOC) has already agreed to postpone the turnaround at its largest refinery, the 192,000-bpd refinery at Koyali where a 50,000-bpd crude distillation unit (CDU) was to shutdown for 22 days in December.
IOC has turnaround plans for five of its six refineries in this remaining fiscal year which ends in March 1997 but most of them were already scheduled for February 1997.

In addition to the 18-day shutdown in January-February of its 60,000-bpd CDU No.2 at the 152,000-bpd Mathura refinery, IOC had planned to bring down in February, a 30,000-bpd CDU for seven days at the 67,000-bpd Barauni refinery in the northeast.
A 20,000-bpd Guwahati refinery will also be down for 15 days and the 55,000-bpd refinery in Haldia for ten days.
State-owned Cochin Refineries Ltd has similarly plans in February to shut down its larger CDU 90,000-bpd at its 150,000-bpd Ambalamugal refinery for 25-30 days.
Refinery turnaround plans for the next fiscal year, April 1997-March 1998 have yet to be finalised, said sources at the government Oil Coordination Committee.
